title: Confidence-Weighted Supervision: Does Overseer Self-Reported Certainty Predict Oversight Quality?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If confidence-weighting reduces error propagation, this is a practical low-cost oversight improvement. The chain is plausible but assumes model-reported confidence is well-calibrated, which is itself an open question.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Training a small model with weighted labels is standard ML. Generating confidence scores from an overseer model is straightforward via API logprobs or prompted self-assessment. Accessible with mentor guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Requires setting up an overseer, generating confidence-weighted labels, training a student under multiple weighting schemes, and comparing. Moderately scoped but achievable in 30 hours if limited to one task.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
